title: Mean short-route backup of bilateral neuron pairs remained after weak-edge removal in two adult worm connectomes
abstract: We tested short-route backup in two adult C. elegans brain reconstructions. We kept 180 common neurons and 83 left-right pairs. The score was joint route loss minus summed single-cell route loss, with the same surviving endpoints in all comparisons. For routes of at most three chemical edges, mean net scores were 0.0283% and 0.0294% of intact reachable endpoint pairs. Means stayed above 2,000 degree-binned partner shuffles after removal of edges with fewer than two or three synapses. Pair scores had rank correlation 0.627 across adults with all edges and 0.834 at the three-synapse threshold. Only 28 pairs had positive scores in both adults in the primary test. Bilateral backup is a prior result; this study adds a bounded-route decomposition and a weak-edge test. The result is structural. Two partial brains, coarse degree bins, missing physiology, and a few large pair scores limit its scope. Code, source hashes, all pair counts, shuffle draws, and independent search checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Route loss in two adult worm brains. Solid lines show mean net backup at three edge thresholds; dotted lines and shading show the degree-binned partner-shuffle mean and central 95% range. The middle panel separates backup from serial dependence. The right panel compares pair scores across adults. The ranges are conditional shuffle ranges, not animal confidence intervals.
